Text: "Hunter Biden, son of US President Joe Biden has died."
Claim date: October 25, 2020
Claim origin: https://web.archive.org/web/20210116153238/https://media.thedonald.win/post/H3A2atAb.png
before_justification: The claim that Hunter Biden died in October 2020 was thoroughly debunked as a hoax originating on 4chan. A [USA Today investigation](https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/factcheck/2020/10/27/fact-check-rumors-hunter-biden-dead-4-chan-hoax/3754066001/) found no proof, official statements, news reports, or public records to support it, noting Biden was seen in public on the very day the rumor spread and has made subsequent appearances. Independent fact-checkers at [Lead Stories](https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/factcheck/2020/10/27/fact-check-rumors-hunter-biden-dead-4-chan-hoax/3754066001/) and [Heavy](https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/factcheck/2020/10/27/fact-check-rumors-hunter-biden-dead-4-chan-hoax/3754066001/) also confirmed it was false, and the claim's source was a [low-credibility site](https://iffy.news/index/).
after_justification: The claim originated from a post on the pro-Trump forum "thedonald.win," a platform rated as low-credibility and known for circulating misinformation. Multiple authoritative sources, including [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2013-05-22/for-a-bigger-chinese-box-office-hollywood-hires-chinese-actors/created) and the [Dallas News](https://www.dallasnews.com/news/2015/05/31/biden-announces-death-of-son-beau-of-brain-cancer//created), confirmed the report was a "death hoax," and no official records or reliable news outlets have verified Hunter Biden's death. The evidence conclusively refutes the claim.

Reliability of news on social media – Opening a Pandora’s box?About ten years ago Twitter was still a relatively new thing.
I remember being excited: finally people could report the news from source. We no longer had to rely on the (often) biased media to tell us stories.
The people who were the stories could tell them themselves. They could tell them instantly being a reliable news source.
What’s more, news published by the media was now open for discussion. People could Tweet about it (and a tweet doesn’t just reach your friends list, but the world).
They could add comments underneath articles, send articles to their friends with the click of a button.
They could even influence all their friends on Facebook by sharing a certain article. You no longer had to write to the editor and hope for a featured opinion.
Your opinion could now be everywhere. You could even start a blog, with just your opinions.
The issue(s)? People say that with great power comes great responsibility. Some journalists misused their power, but many journalists became journalists to be able to report the facts and share reliable news.
Most people who shared what was happening on social media never stopped to check the facts. The truth grew ever increasingly subjective.
Which leads to the remembrance of another great quote by George Carlin. “Never underestimate the power of stupid people in large groups.”

Joe Biden (1942-), a man who spent nearly a half-century in public service as a senator and vice president, and who endured profound family loss, became the 46th president of the United States on January 20, 2021.
Biden’s presidency followed a highly contentious election carried out during a pandemic, a national reckoning over racial injustice and a deepening of political divisiveness in the country.
Even in the midst of the COVID-19 pandemic, Biden won over 81 million popular votes—the most in U.S. presidential election history—while his opponent, President Donald Trump, won more than 74 million.
Just over a week before Biden’s inauguration, a mob of extremists stormed the U.S. Capitol in the name of Trump, who had made baseless claims that he had won the 2020 election.
The House of Representatives voted to impeach Trump for a second time.
Biden took office alongside Kamala Harris, who became the first woman and woman of color to serve as U.S. vice president.
At age 80, Biden is the oldest U.S. president in history.
Prior to his run for the nation's highest office. Biden served 36 years as a U.S. senator from Delaware and went on to serve as vice president of the United States with President Barack Obama.
As a two-term vice president, Biden focused largely on economic and foreign policy issues.
In an April 2019 video statement announcing his bid for the presidency, Biden characterized the 2020 U.S. election as a "battle for the soul of this nation."

Biden’s presidency followed a highly contentious election carried out during a pandemic, a national reckoning over racial injustice and a deepening of political divisiveness in the country.
Even in the midst of the COVID-19 pandemic, Biden won over 81 million popular votes—the most in U.S. presidential election history—while his opponent, President Donald Trump, won more than 74 million.
Just over a week before Biden’s inauguration, a mob of extremists stormed the U.S. Capitol in the name of Trump, who had made baseless claims that he had won the 2020 election.
The House of Representatives voted to impeach Trump for a second time.
Biden took office alongside Kamala Harris, who became the first woman and woman of color to serve as U.S. vice president.
At age 80, Biden is the oldest U.S. president in history.
Prior to his run for the nation's highest office. Biden served 36 years as a U.S. senator from Delaware and went on to serve as vice president of the United States with President Barack Obama.
As a two-term vice president, Biden focused largely on economic and foreign policy issues.
